data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference is defensible only by accepting a non-probabilistic metaphysical commitment to verisimilitude (truth-likeness), arguing that severe testing logically increases a theory's proximity to truth despite the inability to verify this progress.","counterconditions":[{"case":"refuted if it can be shown that the concept of 'verisimilitude' cannot be formally defined without implicitly relying on inductive probability","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"refuted if a rigorous demonstration shows that a coherent, non-probabilistic measure of verisimilitude exists which successfully ranks theories such that higher corroboration strictly implies greater closeness to the truth","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"refuted if Popper explicitly distinguished 'verisimilitude' as a logical relation of content comparison rather than a predictive expectation","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Shifting the goal from 'predictive reliability' to 'structural approximation' allows the preference to survive anti-induction critique, but costs the framework its claim to pure logic by smuggling in a rationalist faith that nature rewards boldness.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
